reason: The public proposition is clear and the supplied desktop/mobile hero captures show coherent Precision Instrument hierarchy and generous primary controls. Source inspection of the client inquiry journey and application recovery journey shows native inputs/buttons, associated validation messages, explicit copy selection, focused recovery headings, and honest save/submit uncertainty. Original-resume access is disclosed rather than called anonymous; unavailable case studies are not replaced with invented outcomes. However, the operator discussion screen explicitly bypasses reduced-motion protection. This prevents an unqualified world-class accessibility judgment. Hold for that correction and focused verification. This is a simulated AI accessibility review of frozen source, supplied captures and local test evidence, not observed user success or accessibility certification.

findings.evidence: The reduce media query at lines 569-577 deliberately excludes .deck-root and its descendants. Lines 522-566 define fly/spin/swoosh entrances, infinite drumroll/shimmer, headshot pop, screen shake, confetti and infinite pulse. DeliberationDeck applies deck-root, entrance attributes, deck-headshot-pop, deck-wordart and deck-pulse. Only the numeric count-up separately checks the preference (line 63); the CSS effects remain active.
findings.userImpact: An operator or meeting attendee requesting reduced motion still encounters large card motion and repeating effects while reading consequential applicant evidence. A projected display also exposes attendees who do not control the presenting computer.
findings.suggestedFix: Include the deck in reduced-motion overrides and render static final states. Provide a persistent presentation motion-off control for shared displays. Verify card navigation, reveal, and revisit flows with reduced motion enabled, including computed animation styles.

notVerified: No live authenticated journey, hosted Clerk/Supabase/storage/email integration, staging environment, or human usability study exists in the supplied evidence.
No screen-reader announcement testing, switch/voice access, physical-device touch testing, Safari/Firefox validation, zoom/reflow audit, or formal accessibility conformance assessment was performed.

The application tests use synthetic fixtures and mostly programmatic clicks/fills. They establish sampled recovery state transitions, not a complete keyboard-only retry journey or reliable announcement order after upload/submission controls are disabled and re-enabled.

Public-journey tests cover menu Escape/focus return, mocked inquiry confirmation and instrument reduced-motion styles; the supplied 76-pass log does not establish accessibility across every private workflow. Private recovery screens have no supplied visual captures inspected here.
